## What kind of change does this PR introduce?

Bug fix

## What is the current behavior?

Closes #11656

## What is the new behavior?

Actually, when self-hosting Supabase, we can change `SUPABASE_PUBLIC_URL` to tell Supabase where to find Kong and all other services. The fact is that the address is not taken in consideration due to some bugs.
First the protocol to be used is evaluated at build time, so when the Docker image is built, not good.
Second the endpoint is also evaluated at buildtime, but this is due to this PR #11331.
The commits that introduced this bug are: https://github.com/supabase/supabase/commit/0868ee96f27333cd541dd5d512368a584a510210 and https://github.com/supabase/supabase/commit/3070064cc54b82a84c5eff4810170e40277e772d
Those commit are simply wrong because they are trying to pull serverside data into clientside at runtime and it doesn't work like this, this data is "translated" at builtime.
Instead the correct pattern is to pass down the protocol via props like proposed in this PR.
I thought we can evaluate the protocol based on the protocol on the frontend, but it won't work 100%.

## Additional context

Add any other context or screenshots.

issue_context.title: Self-Hosted Studio makes requests to `localhost:8000` instead of `EXTERNAL_API_URL`
issue_context.body:
# Bug report

## Describe the bug

When loading tables and buckets, the `Studio` makes requests to `http://localhost:8000/storage/v1/bucket` and `http://localhost:8000/rest/v1/` instead of `https://kong.example.com/rest/v1/`. This means that if I visit the `Studio` externally it will be stuck on `Connecting to default project` because only the host computer can reach `localhost`.

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior, please provide code snippets or a repository:

1. Clone the master branch
2. Create subdomains that point to point `8000` and `3000`
3. Use the subdomain that points to `8000` as `API_EXTERNAL_URL` and `SUPABASE_PUBLIC_URL`  in `.env`
4. `docker compose up -d`
5. Visit the `3000` subdomain on the host computer and it works but you will see in `Network` that the requests are made to `localhost:8000`
6. Visit the `3000` subdomain on a different computer and it does not work,
    - You will see in `Network` that the requests are made to `localhost:8000`
    - External computer cannot reach that
    - Everthing will show `Connecting to default project`

## Expected behavior

The `Studio` should use the correct URL to make requests.

## Screenshots

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/109893647/212433889-24dde24a-02aa-4ccb-9f81-4b259c81a410.png)

## Additional context

I know that this is a bug and not an issue with my configuration because it worked before AND my configuration still works when I run the `Studio` locally. According to [a comment on a separate bug fix](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/pull/11331#issuecomment-1375561791), this bug was introduced a few weeks ago on the docker image.
comments:
Hi @globemediaofficial,
you sure it worked before? Because from what I know, you have to rebuild the studio image in Docker if you want to change the Endpoint for rest and storage calls.
This is because NextJs evaluates environment variables at build time, so when building the studio image.
From what I've read in your issue template you are using the default studio image.
I suggest you to try building the image locally and use it in the docker compose file.
Let me know if I'm wrong or it has worked

@ruggi99 
I’m not sure what you mean. Yes, it worked before. From what I understand, the endpoints come from `.env` which I have set up so there is no reason to build a local image, unless the instructions have changed. I am using the `20230112-a2ba827` image from 5 days ago.

Ok, but what I'm saying is that you probably have to set up environment variables before building the studio image, IMO.
In NextJS environment variables are not read runtime at client side and from what I've seen, the environment variables you are using are client side. So they are "injected" at buildtime

> Ok, but what I'm saying is that you probably have to set up environment variables before building the studio image, IMO.
> In NextJS environment variables are not read runtime at client side and from what I've seen, the environment variables you are using are client side. So they are "injected" at buildtime

@ruggi99 
I used `Docker compose down` and then `Docker compose up -d` which has always worked for me in the past when I changed variables.

@serebano, what you found is true but it doesn't fit in this issue.

Now I found why it may have broke and why it worked before as said by @globemediaofficial 
Actually I think that your PR #11331 broke this behavior because you changed the first line in `constants.ts`.

Now we are using `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLIC_URL` and it is known that it is evaluated at build time, where `SUPABASE_PUBLIC_URL` is evaluated at runtime. So we should revert that change to make it working again.
This is why `constants.ts` is used server side and it makes no sense to use a client side environmente variable

I'v read your PR template and I don't get why it wasn't working for you (you said that it couldn't access the variable).
Can you try reverting that change locally (only `constant.ts` file) and try again?

@ruggi99 in the final version of the PR that was merged, the `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLIC_URL` exists, but it was only added. It was added because a different PR tried to access  `SUPABASE_PUBLIC_URL` which it could not. Adding the new variable did fix that mixed content issue. `SUPABASE_PUBLIC_URL` is still there, it wasn’t removed, so I don’t see how that could be an issue.
So if you read again my message, I'm saying that you changed the `contants.ts` file, not `.env` file. I think the error is that change

Ok, I think I've understood the problem going on.
The fact is, simplying a bit, that the protocol to be used for only storage and rest routes is calculated at buildtime (at buildtime the env var is always `http://localhost:8000` and therefore always http as you said).

To fix this I will send a PR where the protocol is calculated at runtime clientside and I hope will fix it.
As you said, the commit https://github.com/supabase/supabase/commit/0868ee96f27333cd541dd5d512368a584a510210 is the source of the problem because of the difference between builtime and runtime (didn't noticed yesterday).

But your PR still needs to be reverted because is a no-op fix.

Sorry for the inconvenience, will try to explain me better in the PR template.

review_comments: Hmm we try to keep this static api response symmetric with what our platform api returns. This change would make the static api response different from that of platform...

Yes I know, but the protocol is ignored when using the platform. Maybe adding a static "https" return from the platform?
Maybe should I add a comment explaining why it is needed?

This will be undefined in our production API. 

My preference is to retain the same API format for both self hosted and prod. With this PR, we add a field to only the self hosted API and not the production one which would lead to bugs only in one environment (like this one being undefined in production). Not opposed to adding a protocol field, but lets do it internally too.

Yes we know it will be undefined in production, but also it's always bypassed in production.
It doesn't lead to bugs for now but it'll be in the future due to the mismatch of the API (for example someone modifies code without knowing the mismatch).
So for now it is safe.
Also if you add the protocol field it is safe to remove all conditionals, for example: `{IS PLATFORM ? "https" : protocol}`
yeah that would be ideal @sweatybridge - adding it to the prod api, wdyt?
Sounds good. I will update our api next week
